Most proofs are short and clear. The one clear simplification is the integral-congruence tail of referenceSelf_frozenCenteredCoefficient. I could not run Lean, so the replacement is untested. findings.problem: The proof first builds a pointwise equality `hp (z)` of packet values. It then needs `congr 1`, `integral_congr_ae`, `filter_upwards []`, and a hand-written `congrArg` lambda that restates the whole integrand with `f` in place of the packet value. The lambda duplicates the integrand and has to be kept in sync with the `change` statement. The packet in the integrand is the closed term `(Q).physicalPacket t j l u k`, which does not depend on the integration variable. So the equality of Schwartz maps itself can be rewritten, and no pointwise equality, a.e. argument or integrand restatement is needed.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace lines 70–78 by:
  have hp := P.referenceFamily_physicalPacket t t R cone w F hw hcone hF hwide hfrequency j l u k
  rw [hp]
If the unification is fragile, `simp only [hp]` is an alternative. Either way the proof is: after the `change`, replace the narrow-family packet by the original packet using the existing lemma.
findings.benefit: This removes about six lines of integrand duplication and measure-theoretic boilerplate. The reader sees that the proof is a single rewrite by `referenceFamily_physicalPacket`, and the statement of the integrand lives only in the `change`. It also matches how the sibling proof in PacketDataCoefficient ends with `rw [hp]` after unfolding.
